title: A RRAM-based High Energy-efficient Accelerator Supporting Multimodal Tasks for Virtual Reality Wearable Devices
problem: VR wearable devices struggle to efficiently execute multiple simultaneous multi-modal tasks due to severe constraints on battery life and limited hardware resources.
motivation: Immersive VR experiences require fusing tasks from multiple sensory modalities concurrently, but battery and hardware constraints of wearables make this infeasible with current approaches.
method: MTVR has a computing core that efficiently divides its processing power to run multiple different types of tasks (like audio and video processing) in parallel on VR wearables. It saves power through three techniques: an early exit detector that stops processing invalid inputs; fine-grained value skipping at the multiplier and adder level (skipping arithmetic when operands won't affect the result); and a hybrid RRAM-SRAM memory that does computations right where data is stored (compute-in-memory), reducing expensive external memory accesses.
key_novelty: The core idea pairs approximation shortcuts (early exit and value skipping) with a hybrid RRAM-SRAM memory design that performs calculations where data is stored (compute-in-memory), enabling multiple task types to run simultaneously on battery devices with minimal power consumption.
contributions: Multi-task computing core design achieving 95% computational utilization through efficient unit allocation
Early exit detector achieving 88% energy savings when 90% of inputs are invalid
Fine-grained tiny value skip method at multiplier and adder levels saving 13% additional energy
Hybrid RRAM-SRAM memory access scheme reducing external memory access by 98.9%

metrics.other: 95% computational utilization, 88% energy savings (90% invalid inputs), 98.9% EMA reduction

limitations: Limitations not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Energy-efficient multi-modal accelerator for VR wearables
